question: Can a cross-validation-tuned, class-balanced LightGBM classifier choose a better per-instance local-search parameter setting than a standard MLP configuration predictor on generated knapsack instances, judged by the same held-out solution quality?
method: Generated 0/1 knapsack instances (fixed seed) with per-setting local-search quality measured under a fixed evaluation budget; MLP baseline (classifier) vs CV-tuned ensemble of per-setting LightGBM and ExtraTrees quality regressors (row-centred targets, greedy/LP-bound features) choosing the highest predicted setting; test set from a shifted instance family; evaluated by mean normalised solution quality.
metric_name: mean normalised solution quality (value / optimum) on held-out test instances
baseline: Standard MLPClassifier (64-32 hidden, scaled features) predicting the local-search setting
improved: Equal-weight ensemble of per-setting LightGBM and ExtraTrees quality regressors on base plus scale-free greedy/LP-bound features, row-centred targets, 3-fold CV-tuned on training quality, seed-averaged; choose the setting with highest predicted quality
notes: Labels are noisy (single small grid, budget-limited search). The improved model uses the full per-setting quality information from training rather than only the argmax label, so it is not tied to label noise. Improvements over the previous version: scale-free greedy/LP-bound features (improved model only), row-centred regression targets (argmax unchanged), and an LightGBM+ExtraTrees ensemble. Test family is shifted in size and correlation, so tree models cannot extrapolate in size; the scale-free features are meant to help with this. Test set used once for both models; tuning used only training CV. Results depend on the generator and budget and are not a replication of OPTICAT's deep RL results.
